The Extra Equipment in Your Frisco Weekend: Glasses, Contacts, and Everything That Comes With Them

Explore how everyday routines can shape a conversation about LASIK and SMILE.

Lifestyle & vision · September 30, 2026

Some weekend equipment is easy to remember: walking shoes, a water bottle, a cap.

Other equipment follows you everywhere without making the packing list. Prescription glasses. Contact lenses. A spare pair. The case and solution you hope you remembered.

For people who wear corrective lenses, an active Frisco weekend can come with a little extra planning. Glasses slide during a workout. Prescription sunglasses become another purchase. An overnight bag needs more than a toothbrush.

None of these inconveniences means surgery is necessary. But together, they explain why some people begin exploring vision correction.

Start with your routine

Before comparing procedures, consider what you want to make easier.

Do you want less dependence on glasses during exercise? Fewer contact lens supplies when traveling? Less switching between everyday glasses and prescription sunglasses?

Those goals are useful starting points for a consultation. They give an eye surgeon more context than simply saying, “I want better vision.”

LASIK and SMILE take different approaches

LASIK and SMILE are laser vision correction procedures that change the shape of the cornea. LASIK uses a corneal flap; SMILE removes a small piece of tissue through a small incision without creating that flap.

The right choice depends on your prescription, eye health, corneal measurements, and other factors. A procedure that worked well for a friend may not be the best fit for you.

For residents considering their options, LaserCare Eye Center’s Frisco office offers information about LASIK, SMILE, and other approaches to vision correction.

Plan recovery as carefully as the weekend

Ask about risks, expected recovery, and when you can return to your particular activities. Dry eye symptoms, glare, halos, and continued need for glasses are among the issues worth discussing.

Surgery also does not replace sunglasses or protective sports eyewear. Reducing dependence on prescription lenses and protecting your eyes are separate goals.

The most useful question is not which procedure sounds newest. It is which option—if any—fits your eyes and the life you want to enjoy around Frisco.
